AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is compost manure? (1 mark)
   A. Fertiliser made in a factory
   B. A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   C. Fresh soil from a river bank
   D. A kind of animal feed

2. Where is the best place to make a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. In the middle of a stream
   B. A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   C. Inside the kitchen
   D. In a very windy open road

3. Why is a compost heap turned with a fork? (1 mark)
   A. To remove all the water
   B. To let in air and mix the materials
   C. To add plastic
   D. To make it smaller

4. Which of these crops can be watered with drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Only crops under water
   B. Tomatoes in rows
   C. Nothing at all
   D. Only trees in forests

5. Why does drip irrigation save water? (1 mark)
   A. It wets the paths between plants
   B. It waters at midday
   C. It uses more water than a hose
   D. Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted

6. Which of these can be used to keep boiled water hot? (1 mark)
   A. An open basin
   B. A thermos flask
   C. A metal spoon
   D. A hot stone

7. What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished? (1 mark)
   A. Pour paraffin on it
   B. Put it out
   C. Leave it burning
   D. Add more wood

8. What is poaching? (1 mark)
   A. Feeding wild animals
   B. Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   C. Planting trees
   D. Watering crops

9. Which crop is established by direct sowing of tiny seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Carrot
   C. Sweet potato
   D. Banana

10. Why are weeds removed from the seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. They are colourful
   B. They protect seedlings from rain
   C. They take water, light and food from the crop
   D. They add manure

11. Which sign shows that a guava is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. It has flowers on it
   B. It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   C. It is dark green and hard
   D. It is dry and black

12. Which of these is a climbing fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Guava
   C. Orange
   D. Mango

13. What can an agricultural extension officer help with? (1 mark)
   A. Selling your tools
   B. Cooking meals
   C. Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   D. Building a house

14. Which of these is a fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Cabbage
   B. Spinach
   C. Sukuma wiki
   D. Guava

15. Which is a pest problem for ripe fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Stones
   B. Sand
   C. Fruit flies and birds
   D. Sun

16. Which nutrient in milk builds strong bones and teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Starch
   B. Calcium
   C. Salt
   D. Sugar

17. Which of these can oxen do on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. Lay eggs
   B. Give wool
   C. Pull ploughs and carts
   D. Produce honey

18. What is the young one of a goat called? (1 mark)
   A. Chick
   B. Kid
   C. Lamb
   D. Calf

19. What do body-building foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Help the body to grow and repair
   B. Only quench thirst
   C. Make food taste sweet
   D. Only give heat

20. How much oil is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   B. A full pot
   C. None
   D. A whole bottle

21. Why should you wear clean clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To get tired
   B. To save water
   C. Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   D. To make the clothes wear out

22. Which PPE protects the nose and mouth from dust? (1 mark)
   A. Overall
   B. Gloves
   C. Dust mask
   D. Gumboots

23. Which is a way of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Burn tins
   B. Throw things away quickly
   C. Reuse containers
   D. Buy more packages

24. Why should food be covered in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it hot forever
   B. To make it heavier
   C. To hide the plate
   D. To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches

25. Why should chemicals not be used to clean PPE unless an adult directs you? (1 mark)
   A. They cool the PPE
   B. They make it too clean
   C. They can harm the skin and the material
   D. They are too cheap

26. What do you use to mark a straight line on cloth? (1 mark)
   A. Chalk and a ruler
   B. A plate
   C. A broom
   D. A hammer

27. When is long and short tacking a good choice? (1 mark)
   A. For curves only
   B. For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough
   C. For hems on very slippery cloth
   D. It is never used

28. What is one purpose of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. To iron cloth
   B. To wash cloth
   C. To hold layers of cloth together before sewing
   D. To cut cloth

29. How should you carry scissors? (1 mark)
   A. By the blades
   B. Running
   C. With the points up
   D. With the points held down

30. About how long is each stitch in even tacking in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm
   B. 1 mm
   C. 1 cm
   D. 1 metre

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain two mistakes that can spoil a newly planted fruit tree and how to avoid them. (4 marks)

32. Give three reasons why nails should be kept short and clean. (3 marks)

33. What is personal protective equipment (PPE)? (2 marks)

34. Give two advantages of boiling food. (2 marks)

35. Explain the steps for dusting a room. (4 marks)

36. Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment. (5 marks)

37. Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced. (3 marks)

38. Explain three safety rules when cleaning. (3 marks)

39. Explain the difference between green and brown materials for compost, with an example of each. (3 marks)

40. Why do we dust before sweeping? (2 marks)

41. Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced. (5 marks)

42. Give two ways of protecting fruits from birds and monkeys without killing them. (2 marks)

43. Explain how to sow tiny seeds in a drill. (4 marks)

44. Describe how to make a scarecrow. (4 marks)

45. How can a family get a balanced meal cheaply? (2 marks)

46. State the difference between boiling and shallow frying. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   Compost is organic manure made from rotted wastes.

2. B — A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   A shaded, dry spot protects the heap from sun and flooding.

3. B — To let in air and mix the materials
   Mixing brings outer material to the middle so all rots evenly.

4. B — Tomatoes in rows
   Drip systems suit row crops such as tomatoes and kale.

5. D — Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   Only the soil near the plant is wet, so less water is lost.

6. B — A thermos flask
   A flask keeps water hot so it need not be boiled again.

7. B — Put it out
   Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

8. B — Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   Poaching is against the law.

9. B — Carrot
   Carrots are sown directly because transplanting damages their roots.

10. C — They take water, light and food from the crop
   Weeds compete with crops.

11. B — It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   Ripe guavas change colour and smell sweet.

12. A — Passion fruit
   Passion fruit needs support to climb.

13. C — Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   Extension officers advise farmers.

14. D — Guava
   Guava is a fruit.

15. C — Fruit flies and birds
   Ripe fruit attracts flies and birds.

16. B — Calcium
   Milk has calcium and protein.

17. C — Pull ploughs and carts
   Oxen give draught power.

18. B — Kid
   A young goat is a kid.

19. A — Help the body to grow and repair
   They are rich in protein.

20. A — A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer.

21. C — Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   Clean clothes keep us fresh.

22. C — Dust mask
   A dust mask covers the nose and mouth.

23. C — Reuse containers
   Reuse cuts down rubbish.

24. D — To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches
   Covered food is protected.

25. C — They can harm the skin and the material
   Chemicals can be dangerous.

26. A — Chalk and a ruler
   Chalk marks show the line.

27. B — For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough
   It is quicker.

28. C — To hold layers of cloth together before sewing
   Tacking keeps layers in place.

29. D — With the points held down
   This avoids injury.

30. C — 1 cm
   Even tacking uses 1 cm stitches and gaps.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Burying the graft joint under the soil, plant with joint above the ground; not watering in dry weather, water regularly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake and 1 for each solution.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs hide under nails, worm eggs are found there, and long nails can scratch and cause injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Clothing and gear worn to protect the body from dirt, injury, dust and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for clothing or gear, 1 mark for protection.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: It needs no oil and it makes hard food soft and safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open windows; use a slightly damp clean cloth; dust from high to low; shake and wash the duster outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group named.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not mix chemicals; keep chemicals from children; wear gloves for dirty work; do not leave floors wet (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Green materials are fresh and wet such as fresh grass or peelings. Brown materials are dry such as dry leaves or straw.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dust falls to the floor, so sweeping afterwards removes it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dust falls, 1 mark for sweeping removes.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cover with nets, use scarecrows, noise or shiny objects (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a shallow drill about 1 cm deep; mix seeds with sand; sprinkle thinly in the drill; cover lightly with fine soil; water gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix a long pole firmly in the ground; tie a shorter stick across it; put a stuffed head on top; dress with a stuffed shirt and hat; add tins or shiny strips.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Grow vegetables and fruits at home and use cheap proteins such as beans, omena or eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Shallow frying cooks food in a thin layer of hot oil in a pan.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.
